subject: Integration recap: SDK/auth, structured output & congestion resilience
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Yates <tom.yates@datacorp.com>, Alyssa Chen <ops@datacorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Integration recap: SDK/auth, structured output & congestion resilience

Tom / Alyssa — thanks again for the great discussion this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on integration surface areas and how Redwood can help DataCorp avoid operational surprises under load. I kept this focused on the architecture topics we prioritized: SDK setup, auth, routing, structured output / tool-calling, embeddings/rerankers, and congestion/resilience (429s, retries, idempotency).

Key takeaways from call: 
- You want an SDK-first integration to minimize client-side ops work: baked-in auth, request IDs, client-side batching, and helpers for structured-output/tool-calls.
- Security: initial integration must use token auth for hosted POC; Private deployment will be evaluated for production (Data never leaves VPC without approval).
- We should route high-QPS embedding requests to a dedicated embedding pool and keep reranker calls (low QPS, high-precision) on a separate route to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
- For 429/overload handling we discussed: server-side Retry-After, X-Rate-Limit-* headers, and client backoff with full jitter. Idempotency keys for any stateful POST (e.g., re-ranker votes, annotation uploads) were requested.

Proposed recommendations (short):
1) SDK behavior (out of the box):
   - Automatic request ID header: X-Req-Id: rc-{customer}-{short-ts}-{rand6} (visible in logs).
   - Exponential backoff with full jitter on 429/5xx (initial 250ms, cap 10s) and optional circuit-breaker after N sequential 429s.
   - Transparent client-side batching for embedding endpoints (configurable max batch size + max latency).
   - Built-in structured-output helper that validates tool-calling JSON schemas before sending to reduce malformed requests.
2) Auth & routing:
   - POC: API key tokens with shortest practical TTL + audit logs.
   - Prod: recommend Private deployment or dedicated VPC peering for PII-sensitive flows.
   - Route by endpoint: /v1/embeddings -> embedding pool; /v1/re-rank -> reranker pool; /v1/generate -> latency-optimized pool.
3) Rate-limit & retry policy:
   - Honor Retry-After header when present.
   - If no Retry-After, RFC-style exponential backoff with full jitter.
   - Retries only for idempotent operations by default; allow retries for non-idempotent calls only when client supplies Idempotency-Key header.
   - Server will return helpful headers: X-Rate-Limit-Limit, X-Rate-Limit-Remaining, X-Rate-Limit-Reset (epoch).
4) Idempotency & request IDs:
   - Use X-Idempotency-Key for user-level dedupe on stateful calls; TTL on server-side dedupe keys 24h (configurable).
   - X-Req-Id to correlate logs; keep under 64 bytes, UTF-8 safe.
5) Embeddings & reranker notes:
   - Suggested pattern: client issues batch embedding request -> store vector in your vector DB with client-generated object id -> reranker calls supply top-k candidates and use a separate low-QPS dedicated reranker route.
   - Cache TTL for embeddings: point-in-time snapshots should use explicit versioning in IDs so reindexing is safe.

Immediate asks / next steps: 
- Dev: can you share a representative traffic spike profile (QPS over 1-minute / 5-minute windows and typical request sizes)?
- Ops (Alyssa): confirm whether PII classification requires Private deployment for POC or if hosted with token+KMS is acceptable for the initial test.
- Redwood: we will provide a sandbox API key, the SDK pre-release, and an integration checklist. I attached the checklist and our idempotency guidance doc.

Proposed next meeting: 30 minutes next Tuesday to walk through the SDK sample code and the draft retry/queueing behavior. I can set this up once you confirm availability.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Tom Yates <tom.yates@datacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration recap: SDK/auth, structured output & congestion resilience

Thanks Jasmine — quick technical clarifications / asks from our engineering side: 

1) Traffic profile: Tom, please send the 95th/99th percentile QPS for embeddings and re-ranker calls and the typical document size (tokens). This informs batch sizing and KV cache sizing.
2) Request-id format: we recommend rc-{org}-{env}-{tssec}-{rand4}. Total header length must remain <64 bytes. Please confirm whether you need the request-id echoed back on stream chunks for client-side correlation.
3) Idempotency scope: confirm which endpoints you consider "stateful" — from what we heard, you will only mutate annotations/labels via API. We'll enforce retries only when X-Idempotency-Key present. Server-side dedupe TTL default 24h; we can shorten for POC.
4) Structured output: to reduce malformed tool-calls we can include client-side schema validators in the SDK. Are you comfortable publishing your tool schemas (small JSON schema bundle) to the shared Drive link?
5) Fallback behavior: if an embedding pool is saturated, do you want automatic fallbacks to a cheaper quantized model (lower-accuracy) or a strict error so clients can surface to users? We can configure either.

Implementation notes: we will ship an SDK pre-release (Node + Python) with: token auth helper, request-id middleware, retry middleware (configurable), embedding batcher, and a schema validator for tool output. For server-side we will include rate-limit headers and recommend using Retry-After where the driver detects sustained pressure.

Action items: 
- Tom: traffic numbers + confirmation on fallback behavior.
- Alyssa: security constraint confirmation (hosted token ok vs Private).
- Dev (me): will prepare the SDK pre-release and a short design doc for request-id and idempotency flows.

Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Tom Yates <tom.yates@datacorp.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <ops@datacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration recap: SDK/auth, structured output & congestion resilience

Appreciate the clear summary and the proposed defaults. Short answers from our side: 

- Traffic profile (attached): steady-state embeddings ~ 120 QPS, peaks to ~800 QPS for short bursts (1-2 min). Re-ranker calls are ~6 QPS steady, spikes to ~40 QPS. Typical prompt sizes: embeddings payloads ~ 600 tokens, generation prompts ~ 350 tokens.
- Request-id: echoing the request id back in the chunk stream would be very helpful for debugging. The suggested format is fine; keep it compact.
- Fallback: for our UX we prefer automatic fallback to a lower-cost quantized model rather than failing requests, but only for non-critical flows. For critical workflows (search ranking) we'd prefer error so we can surface degraded status. We can flag routes as "critical" vs "best-effort".
- Security: for the POC hosted token with KMS + audit logs is acceptable. For production we will require Private deployment. PII note: none of the initial test data contains sensitive PII, but we will lock that down before prod.

Timeline ask: can you provide a sandbox key and the Node SDK pre-release by EOD next Wednesday (29 Aug)? That gives us one week to smoke test before our internal demo on Sep 7. Also please include a lightweight chaos test (burst generator) so we can reproduce spikes and verify backoff behavior.

Tom Yates
Head of Platform, DataCorp
tom.yates@datacorp.com

Subject: Re: Integration recap: SDK/auth, structured output & congestion resilience

Perfect — thanks Tom, that profile is exactly what we needed. Short confirmation and owners: 

- Sandbox + Node SDK pre-release: Redwood will provide by 2028-08-29 EOD (Dev).
- Chaos test harness (burst generator) + instructions: Redwood ops will include with the sandbox.
- Fallback policy: we'll implement route-level flags for critical vs best-effort; Dev will default to fallback to quantized model for non-critical routes.
- Idempotency & Request-id: Dev will publish the guidelines and we will include X-Req-Id echo in the stream.
- Security: Alyssa to confirm POC hosted token OK; we will circle back on Private deployment timeline during Sep contract discussions.

I scheduled the follow-up 30-minute sync for Tue 2028-08-29 at 10:00am PT — invite sent. If that slot doesn't work I can move it.

Action owners (short):
- Dev Patel: SDK pre-release, idempotency doc, chaos harness (by 2028-08-29 EOD).
- Tom Yates / DataCorp: confirm critical routes list & provide any tool schemas to validate.
- Alyssa Chen: confirm hosted token OK for POC (reply in thread).
- Marissa Cole / Sales: prepare pricing/POC commercial note for Sep review.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the POC.
